meta: Prepared 2026-09-10 for jhan (the PR author), updated 2026-09-11. The findings cite the pre-split head `60d66d9c04`. Every line number on this page refers to `524c510609`, the head Bill approved, unless another tree is named; the PR head moved to `4290402491` on 2026-09-11 02:29 UTC (see the update block below for what shifted). short: Bill's Claude review of 2026-09-05 looked at the pre-split head; six of its 14 findings (3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12) describe code that is no longer in #3879, because the K mirror is parked and the counters merged separately as PR #4267. Of the eight that still touch #3879, the CI blocker is half fixed (the code compiles on every PR build, but execution on AMX hardware is not yet a required check), the tile-region guard and the s_pages stride assert landed in 4290402491 on 2026-09-11, the shared softmax helper was dropped by agreement with Ben, and on three (test fakes, CPU-probe home, V accessors) our position differs. One fact matters more than any finding: #3879 conflicts with main in four files since #4267 merged, so no CI has run on the head Bill approved; a rebase is the first step.
glossary: tron is the inference program under test; runtron is its command-line tool; rinzler is the production server.
AMX (Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions) multiplies small matrices held in 8 tile registers. AVX-512 is the vector instruction set the existing attention code (the dotter loop) uses.

PR 3879 was split on 2026-09-08. PR 0 = #4267 (page-share counters, merged 2026-09-10 00:45 UTC). PR 0b = #4265 (a one-line memory-order fix plus a test, merged 2026-09-10 17:45 UTC). PR 3879 kept its number and now holds only the canonical AMX path. PR 2 = the K mirror arena, a local branch parked as a reference draft, not opened.

The old head `60d66d9c04` is the commit Bill's review cites (35 commits, 18 files, +2538/-52 against base 1407f48dd; the review says 33 commits). The head `524c510609` is the tip of PR 3879 that Bill approved.
A second copy of the attention keys (K) in the tile-friendly VNNI layout, kept in a separate heap allocation (the arena) beside the KV pages. PR 2 only.
Bill's own proposal ("Single-Format VNNI KV", 2026-09-04): store K once, in the VNNI layout, instead of keeping a mirror. A dated gate (2026-09-16) decides between single-K and the mirror.
The CMake option (default OFF) that compiles the AMX kernels and their dispatch. The CMake CI lane builds with it ON since PR 3879's force-push.
A Catch2 test case that passes unconditionally because the code under test is compiled out.
The One Definition Rule of C++: one definition of each non-inline function in a program.
A place where one implementation can be substituted for another without editing the caller; Bill's companion document proposes a template parameter as that seam.
A value tron exposes as a file in its stats file system (FUSE) and, when exported, as a Prometheus metric.
Time to first token, the latency of a request's prefill.
Intel's interleaved bf16-pair layout, the B-operand layout the AMX tile multiply reads.
Group of four: the 4-token staging block the FPGA hardware-attention path builds from K and V (the shuffle into it is the G2 gate measurement).
The existing AVX-512 attention loop (one query-key dot product per token) and the per-page softmax step that follows it.
Catch2 is the C++ test framework; bin/slice is tron's test runner, which schedules test binaries by their recorded cost data and reports pass or fail from the exit code.
lld is the linker the build uses; ThinLTO is link-time optimization applied per target by the `lto` CMake macro.
The instruction that clears a thread's AMX tile configuration; the region is the span between begin_region() (load) and end_region() (release).
The repository's generic scope guard (h/common/util.hpp:73): an object whose destructor runs the stored callable.
book is the per-model KV cache object; a page holds 64 tokens; kv_block is the storage struct for one page of one (slot, kv_head): its K and V arrays hold that page's keys and values.
Speculative decoding with a draft model; the draft scheduler shares the validator's root node.
The two gate measurements due 2026-09-16: G1 = cost of storing K in the VNNI layout; G2 = cost of the GOF shuffle from that layout.

comment:
Thanks for the findings document. It reviewed 60d66d9c04, the pre-split head; #3879 was force-pushed on 2026-09-08 and now holds only the canonical AMX path (14 files, +1364/-32). Here is where each item stands at 524c510609, the head you approved.

Not in this PR any more
- 3 (FUSE gauge), 4 (runtime eligibility bool), 5 (amx_mirror_aware_cache concept), 8 (mirror coherence), 12 (raw aligned new[]): all K-mirror code. It lives in a local reference draft that is not pushed. The 2026-09-16 gate (VNNI store cost, GOF shuffle cost) decides between that draft and the single-format VNNI K store you proposed; under single-K the draft is dropped. If the mirror lands instead, I agree with your fixes for 3, 4 and 5 (gauge through get_memory_pressure_stats() and gated registration; eligibility as a policy type on book, which deletes the concept and the shim) and will apply them before that PR opens for review.
- 11 (page_share_counters): merged separately as PR #4267 on 2026-09-10, behind the switch you asked for (CMake option, default OFF; compiled by the coverage preset; host test with its own define). Two parts of your fix were not taken: the header is still in h/tron/kernels/ and the exit-time reporter stayed. Issue #4303 (FUSE publication of the counters) is where both can change; tell me where you think the header belongs.

Done or half done here
- 1 (nothing compiles it): the CMake CI lane configures with -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON (.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:367), so the kernel, the dispatch and both tests compile on every PR build. Execution on AMX hardware is still not a required check: the runner pool mixes Granite Rapids and Genoa hosts, and the kernel cases warn and return on a host without AMX. #3997 stays open for a pinned job and a required check. The GNUmakefile still has no -D passthrough; the developer path is cmake -B gen --preset native -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON. One number: about 1435 of the 2538 lines (57 %, est.) were behind the options at 60d66d9c04, not all of them.
- 2 (tests assert nothing): two of the four tests remain (t_amx_numerics, t_amx_dispatch_dtype); both have cost data (config/test-benchmarks.json:472-473) and run for real in CI. A default local build still compiles them to SUCCEED stubs; Catch2 SKIP() with the skip_return_code_4 convention would report them as skipped, and I can add that.
- 10 (dispatch woven through the loop): the dense path is one function (apply_dense_amx_page, self_attention.hpp:1471-1542, called at :1604) and the K_MIRROR nesting is gone, but six #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH blocks (seven at the head you approved; the region-close block went with the guard in 4290402491) plus the #error remain. Removing them needs the seam decision below; tracked as #4343.

Accepted, as follow-ups
- 9 (duplicated softmax step): both facts hold. The static_assert on the s_pages layout landed in 4290402491 (self_attention.hpp:1500-1502). The duplication stays: Ben and I compared the two paths in a walkthrough and agreed to keep the split (his thread 3936986164, resolved 2026-09-11).
- 14 (manual tile-region bracket): agreed and done in 4290402491: a tron::finally guard declared next to begin_region() (self_attention.hpp:1352-1354) releases the tile configuration on every exit, and the explicit end_region() block is gone. One count: the loop has three continue paths, not four.
- 7, the Note: agreed. Note [AMX attention dispatch] will say why AMX is a run-time decision while AVX-512 is a configure-time whole-target flag.

Where we see it differently
- 6 (test fakes): the linked test program holds one definition of each entry point, because lld never extracts amx_attn.cpp.o from libtron.a while the test TU defines all six. A seventh kernel function without a fake fails loudly at link time (duplicate symbols). I found no mechanism by which lto(tron) changes this (ThinLTO on tron only; archive members follow the same extraction rule). The --wrap is PR-2 code, and a stale wrap cannot make t_amx_arena_leak skip the arena: its checks assert the allocation happened. Two conventions are unenforced and will be written into the test header: every declared entry point has a fake, and every kernel body stays in the one -mamx TU.
- 7 (probe home): for this PR the probe stays hand-written in the kernel TU: cpuid_bit covers only the CPUID step, and XGETBV and arch_prctl have no helper in system/. A system/ home is reasonable as a follow-up, with one caveat: a namespace-scope lazy<bool> would issue the arch_prctl request at static initialization in every binary that links it, where today it runs at the first dispatch. Three predicates at head (shape_ok, query_scalar_ok, eligible = both), not four; mirror_write_ok is PR-2 code.
- 13 (V accessors): the pair-interleaved V layout predates this PR (main, 2024-11); v_data and v_base are const and their single caller is inside the #ifdef block. I would guard them by the layout's own condition (move them into the existing #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 blocks, no new preprocessor) and add the static_assert at the call site, because the kernel TU includes only the interface header by design.

Companion "AMX Backend Seam": reachable and sound for this PR (t_amx_dispatch_dtype calls apply_page_range directly, so a defaulted backend type parameter lets it pass a fake type). It settles the PR-1 half of 6 and is the prerequisite for 10; it does not touch 3, 4, 5 (not in this PR) or 7 (probe home, predicate count). About 80 lines over 6 files (est., not built). If we take it, the slot is the first follow-up after this PR merges.

Your two inline comments (hugepage arena): answered on the thread on 2026-09-11; in more words, agreed on the direction. The paragraph and the arena are not in #3879 any more. The arena was ordinary RAM so it would not reduce the KV page count; that is also what hid it from the governor and produced the round-1 soak result (43.8-44.6 GB per tp2 engine). If the mirror is reconsidered, the copy moves into the hugepage pool, either as a third plane inside kv_block as your bill-amx branch does, or as a separate pool allocation through try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite; under single-K the question disappears.

Housekeeping: #3879 currently conflicts with main in four files (next to the #4267 hooks), so CI has not run on the recent heads; a rebase is coming. doc/amx_software_attention.md was removed in 47f6f2dceb at Ben's request; environment variables go into one document (#4338).

findings.quote: Both CMake options default OFF. There is no CI reference to TRON_AMX*, no Makefile or preset passthrough to turn them on, and the author's own TODO says so. 2538 lines merge as dead code that will bit-rot against every refactor of self_attention.hpp.

findings.verdict_old_text:
The core claim was true. At 60d66d9c04 no CI job, CMake preset or GNUmakefile rule set TRON_AMX_DISPATCH or TRON_AMX_K_MIRROR, and the TODO comment at src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:170-173 said so (the finding cites :169, one line early). The dev, test and prod configure rules of the GNUmakefile carry a fixed list of -D flags and no passthrough variable [old head GNUmakefile:323, :330, :342]. Three Granite Rapids runners were already listed in README.ci.md:176-178, so the fix needed a configure flag and a runner label, not new hardware.

The line count is over-stated. Of the 2538 added lines, about 1435 (57 %, est.) sat behind the options: the 270-line kernel translation unit (compiled only inside if(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH)), about 1083 lines inside TRON_AMX_* preprocessor conditionals, and about 82 lines behind TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS, which no CMake option defined at that commit. The interface header, whose predicates kv_cache.hpp:186 called in every build, the test scaffolding and the CMake lines compiled everywhere. The counting script tracks #if nesting over the added lines and does not evaluate #elif chains, hence the estimate label.
findings.action: Offer the Intel-pinned CI job; decide on the Makefile passthrough; correct the line count.
findings.now_text:
The compile half is fixed. The build job of the CMake CI lane configures with -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON, so the kernel translation unit, the dispatch blocks and both AMX tests compile whenever that job's build step runs (a restored build cache skips it). README.ci.md documents this, the option moved to the top-level CMakeLists.txt (still default OFF, by design), and the TODO was narrowed to "make one real-AMX test execution a required CI check" with #3997 as the tracker. The default-OFF build is still exercised by the scheduled bench-refresh workflow, so switching the lane to ON did not remove OFF-build coverage.

The execution half is open. The build and test-host jobs run on the label set [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512], which mixes Intel Granite Rapids hosts (AMX) with AMD Genoa hosts (no AMX); a further runner in the delphi family, delphi-3af6-0, serves the same labels without being in the README table (its CPU is not recorded in any repo file; the CI log of run 34375107972 shows an Intel Xeon 6962P). The two kernel cases of t_amx_numerics run AMX only on an Intel host and otherwise warn and return, which counts as a pass. The GNUmakefile still has no generic -D passthrough; the developer path is a direct cmake configure with -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON (the doc page that carried the recipe was removed in 47f6f2dceb). Compile coverage: resolved by the CI flag; this supersedes the earlier triage decision R1-58 ("deferred to #3997"). Execution on AMX hardware: open. Correct the line count without arguing. Drop the "other default-OFF options also lack CI" rebuttal (five of the six other top-level default-OFF options had no workflow reference at 60d66d9c04; COVERAGE did): true, but it does not answer Bill's sentence and reads as deflection. Under the gate: single-K drops the K_MIRROR option; if the mirror lands, the same configure line gets -DTRON_AMX_K_MIRROR=ON plus PR 2's --wrap test.

findings.title: Four tests assert nothing in the default build

What the problem is, in plain words

  • One file, two shapes. A default build (the option OFF, which is what a developer builds locally) compiles apply_page_range, apply_page_tok and attn_accum without these blocks; the CI lane and the AMX hosts compile them with the blocks. A rename or a signature change made while working in the OFF shape can break the ON shape without the author noticing until the CI lane runs. Finding 1 closed that gap for CI; it is still open for local builds.
  • Reading the hot loop means holding three conditions in mind. At blocks 4 and 6 a reader must combine the preprocessor condition, the per-geometry compile-time condition and the per-process run-time condition to know whether a line executes, and the set-up those lines rely on is 70 lines earlier (block 3) while the guard is 1,300 lines earlier.
  • The nesting is three deep. At the head Bill reviewed it was four to five deep, because the K-mirror choice added a further #ifdef inside the dispatch blocks; that layer left with the mirror.

What is done. The dense-page computation is one function (block 5c), called from one place (block 6); the pack is one helper (block 5a); the region bracket is a scope guard (block 3), which removed the seventh block that used to close the region after the loop. Bill's "single call" half is met.

What remains, and why it is not a mechanical edit. Bill's fix asks for "one call and no preprocessor". The statements can lose their #ifdef: blocks 3, 4 and 6 sit inside member function templates, so an if constexpr on a constexpr flag exported by the interface header (true only when the kernel translation unit is compiled) would discard the AMX branch in OFF builds without instantiating it, and the OFF build would then not reference any kernel symbol; the one trap is amx_on = amx_eligible && available(), which must sit inside the discarded branch rather than behind &&, or an unoptimised OFF build would still need the missing available(). Block 5 could also lose its guard, because member functions of a class template are compiled only when something calls them (not verified by a build). Blocks 1 and 2 cannot: if constexpr is a statement, and a type and a data member are declarations. Either every attn_accum in the OFF build carries an unused 24-byte vector with a destructor, or the slot type has to depend on the build (a conditional alias, or a backend type that provides an empty slot type when the option is off). That last option is Bill's backend seam, which is why the page treats the preprocessor removal and the seam as one decision.

What should stay. The #error guard, until finding 13's static_assert on the V byte layout replaces it: it fires at include time with a readable message, before any template is instantiated.

extra_sections.title: Side question: what CI proves today, and why nothing ran on the approved head
extra_sections.text:
Short version: CI compiles the AMX kernel and both AMX test binaries on every build of this branch and runs both binaries, but its log shows only "passed" per binary, so it cannot show whether the two kernel cases executed AMX instructions or skipped. And no CI has run on 524c510609 at all, because the branch conflicts with main.

What ran. Since the CI flag landed (commit 6a40ff5dbe, 2026-09-07), eleven "CMake and CTest" runs were created on the branch: four completed successfully, three failed in the build step on one stale identifier in t/t_llama_unit.cpp (fixed by ac10408318), and four were cancelled by newer pushes. The four successful runs placed the test-host job on delphi-3af6 twice, on delphi-3bd6 once (both Intel Xeon 6962P hosts whose lscpu flags include amx_tile and amx_bf16) and on andoria-14 once (AMD EPYC, no AMX). CI checks out refs/pull/3879/merge, the merge of the head with main at that moment, not the head itself.

extra_sections.title: The companion document: "AMX Backend Seam"
extra_sections.text:
Bill's second artifact proposes, as its first step, wrapping the kernel entry points in `struct hardware_backend` with static member functions and adding a defaulted type parameter to apply_page_range, so that tests pass a fake type instead of redefining the functions. It says the seam "collapses the four costly findings and both test link hacks at once" under four headings (eligibility, detection, accounting, tests); in the findings page's numbering these are 4 (taking 5 with it), 7, 3 and 6. For 3, 4, 5 and 7 the artifact attributes the collapse to three further steps (eligibility as a policy type on book, the probe moved to system/, the arena bytes reported through get_memory_pressure_stats()), which are the same fixes this page accepts for those findings under the mirror-lands branch. Checked against 524c510609:

Reachable and sound. t_amx_dispatch_dtype builds a model in the test itself and calls apply_page_range directly as a member template (t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:149), with no plugin or virtual boundary in between, so a defaulted backend type parameter lets the test hand in a fake type and delete the six redefinitions at :166-190. apply_page_range is a member function template of self_attention<model>::state with template head `<attention_geometry geometry, typename query_buffer_t>` (self_attention.hpp:1283-1290), and the `const auto& page_range` parameter adds a trailing deduced parameter; the proposal's `template <typename model, typename amx>` does not match that signature. The backend type must go in second position, between geometry and query_buffer_t, or `apply_page_range<geometry, fake_backend>` would bind the fake to query_buffer_t (from the C++ deduction rules; not compiled here). The type has to be threaded through three more member templates on the path to the kernel calls: packed_amx_query (:1426, calls pack_q_group_128x4 at :1434), apply_page_tok (:1551, calls no kernel itself; it forwards to apply_dense_amx_page at :1604) and apply_dense_amx_page (:1473, calls qk_rowmajor_128x4 at :1496 and weights_times_v_128x4 at :1522). Six runtime entry points move onto the type (:1331, :1348, :1415, :1434, :1496, :1522); the constants and constexpr predicates can stay in the namespace. The real backend's members must stay declared-only in the header and defined in the one -mamx TU, or an in-class body would be compiled without the AMX flags in every including file.

What it collapses for #3879. Finding 6, this PR's half: yes (no redefinition, no archive-pull dependence, and the LTO concern goes with it). Finding 10: it is the prerequisite for the "no preprocessor" half (the "single call" half is done), because a no-op backend for OFF builds is the piece that would let the in-loop gates become `if constexpr`; that piece is not built and not estimated. Findings 3, 4, 5: not in #3879 (mirror code); the artifact's further steps for them are answered in those findings' sections. Finding 7: the wrapper step alone does not change the probe's home or the predicate count; the artifact's probe-move step is the follow-up discussed in finding 7. Cost of the wrapper step: about 80 lines over five code files (est., not built): the interface header, the kernel TU, four member templates in self_attention.hpp, the fake struct in t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp, and ten call renames in t_amx_numerics.cpp; plus the two-line comment at t/CMakeLists.txt:589-590, six files in all (the doc sentence went with the doc's removal in 47f6f2dceb). Runtime cost: none expected, static-member calls through a template parameter resolve at compile time; not measured.

Recommendation: a follow-up PR, not #3879 now. The edit is small and mechanical but touches the kernel TU, the interface header, four member templates and both AMX tests, and #3879 carries Bill's approval at this head while Ben's CHANGES_REQUESTED still stands. The seam's value is highest right before the next PR that adds kernel functions, since each new kernel otherwise adds another fake to keep in sync; which PR that is (the mirror, or the single-K path) is decided by the 2026-09-16 gate.

extra_sections.title: Bill's two inline comments: should the mirror arena be a hugepage allocation?
extra_sections.text:
Bill's approval body calls these "two comments outstanding regarding K mirror". They are inline comments 3927086929 and 3927096279 (2026-09-03) on doc/memory_pressure_governor.md line 507 at the old head: "Shouldn't this be a hugepage alloc? I'm trying to keep as much stuff outside of the normal round to keep covo em's from happening. Huge page allocations will have better performance as well. It may not be measurable today, but will be when we have conditions with TLB pressure, which probably only happens under complex customer scenarios." and "If moving work to huge pages adds pressure to the huge page allocations, then the solution should be to add more huge pages." ("covo em's" is quoted as written; it probably means OOM kills.) Update 2026-09-11: jhan replied on the thread at 02:33 UTC (comment 3985437314): "I will keep this in mind when working on AMX improvement. BTW this document is being removed, Ben asked me to create another document which lists all TRON environment variables, tracked at #4338." The longer draft below is therefore optional material for a follow-up, not a pending reply.

Facts. The paragraph and the arena are not in #3879: the file is untouched by the PR, and the arena exists only in the parked draft. The arena was ordinary RAM by design (Note [K mirror parallel arena]: only the CPU reads it, and keeping it outside the hugepage budget keeps the KV page count identical with and without the mirror). That same choice hid it from the memory-pressure governor, which measures committed hugepages, and produced the round-1 soak result: the arena reached 43.8 GB at 30 minutes and a 46.5 GB peak (server-log figures, 10^9 bytes) on one tp2 engine, host used memory grew by up to 42.3 GiB, and the soak monitor raised its 5 GiB growth alert while the AMX-off arm stayed flat with 56 GB of KV in hugepages; Wade's evaluation listed "ungoverned RAM sized at pool/2" as blocking. The KV pages themselves come from a pool of 1 GiB hugepages mapped with MAP_POPULATE at startup, so a pool-backed copy is committed up front and counted by the governor with no new code. The same round measured the mirror arm 17 % (llama-3.1-8b tp2) and 24 % (qwen-3-4b tp4) slower to first token than the canonical arm, at parity on mixtral; the cause is unmeasured (leading hypothesis: the K write-through during prefill), so that number says nothing about page size, and Bill's TLB claim is likewise unmeasured.

Two forms of "hugepage alloc". Form A: a third plane inside kv_block, which is what Bill's own bill-amx branch does (member array k_vnni, written through from save_k); the book's DMA buffer grows by half, no new allocation code, the governor counts it because the book is bigger; kv_block is not templated on kv_mul, so ineligible models would carry the plane unless that is fixed. Form B: a separate allocation from the pool through the helper the book already uses (try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite); keeps the arena plumbing; traps: the helper's "callers must propagate failure" rule, the fault-injection seam's assumption that the helper's "only callers are book::try_create" (h/system/memory.hpp:263-264), the dma_size_bytes() contract and the section-5 accounting cross-check. In both forms the pool grows by half the KV bytes (Bill's "add more huge pages") and the "third memory" paragraph is deleted. Note that bill-amx is not single-K: it keeps row-major k and adds k_vnni as a third plane; single-K (his 2026-09-04 document) drops the second copy entirely.

How the gate changes the question. Under single-K the one K copy lives inside the hugepage-backed KV block and the arena and the hugepage question disappear. If the mirror is reconsidered, the fix is the direction Bill asks for, in form A or B, and the PR's Note [K mirror parallel arena] and this paragraph are rewritten; the PR's Note [Why not replace canonical K] argued against single-K until its unmeasured costs were known: the FPGA GOF staging adapter (G2 measures this), a new AVX fallback reader, the kill switch's same-layout contract, and, in its closing line, the VNNI scatter as the primary store (G1 measures this). G1 and G2 cover two of those four points.
